mismatch.message: simple monster action requires special starting-pet state

summary: The saved JavaScript trace reaches the final screen after the Knight successfully leashes the ridden pony, then stops at the monster-turn boundary. apply.c:use_leash() already implements the mounted-down case and sets the pony m_leashed. C sends the steed through dogmove.c:dog_move(), where dog_goal() returns -2 immediately for u.usteed. Frozen JavaScript has matching dog_move() and dog_goal() branches, but unported_monster_actions.js:assertSimpleActionState() rejects every leashed starting pet before dog_move(), including the currently ridden steed. The actionable source-traced defect is this overbroad preflight refusal; the remaining screen and turn RNG are skipped because of it.

source.branch: After a downward apply-leash action on a mounted, moving Knight, the saddled pony is the hero's u.usteed and has m_leashed set. On its normal post-command monster turn, dog_move() performs its ordinary hunger and inventory checks; absent starvation or conflict, dog_goal() sees mtmp == u.usteed and returns -2, so the steed does not move. The JavaScript preflight must admit this mounted-steed state while retaining refusals for other unsupported leashed pets.
callers: C setup path: cmd.c maps the a/apply command to apply.c:doapply(); its LEASH arm calls use_leash() (apply.c:4297-4299). When the target is u_at() and u.usteed exists with u.dz > 0, use_leash() calls use_leash_core() on u.usteed and returns ECMD_TIME (apply.c:796-801); use_leash_core() sets mtmp->mleashed and obj->leashmon (apply.c:854-859). The frozen JS apply.js doapply()/use_leash() path already performs this state change.

C monster turn: monmove.c:m_move() sends a tame, non-worm monster to dogmove.c:dog_move() (monmove.c:1771-1774); dog_move() calls dog_goal() after its steed, hunger and inventory setup (dogmove.c:1011-1044). The corresponding JS path is allmain.js turn preflight -> unported_monster_actions.js:assertSimpleActionState(), then monmove.js:movePet() -> dogmove.js:dog_move() -> dog_goal(). The guard currently stops execution before the source-supported steed branch.

dogmove.c:dog_move() is called by monmove.c:m_move(); dogmove.c:dog_goal() is called only through dog_move() for this runtime path. Frozen JS dogmove.js exports both functions and mirrors the mounted-steed return path.
dependencies: apply.c:use_leash() and use_leash_core() establish the leashed-steed state that exposes the turn path; the frozen JS implementations match their mounted-down C branch, so they are setup rather than the remaining stop owner.
dogmove.c:dog_hunger() and dog_invent() run before dog_goal() in dog_move(); both are already present in frozen js/dogmove.js. For the recorded fresh pony state they pass through to dog_goal().

dogmove.c:dog_goal() checks mtmp == u.usteed before goal calculation and returns -2 without a goal draw (lines 494-496); frozen js/dogmove.js has the same check (line 892). This early return makes the selected leashed-steed state source-supported without opening ordinary leashed-pet movement.

evidence: Saved diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v14/knight-applies-leash-down.json reports 26 emitted screens of 27 and stops on key > with “simple monster action requires special starting-pet state”; the last displayed message is “You slip the leash around your saddled pony.” The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260929225551-v14.json reports 26/27 screens and 2771/2784 RNG calls. The manifest labels the preceding source action apply.c:use_leash mounted-steed downward arm; source tracing below identifies the later turn gate that actually stops replay.

C state setup: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:769-817 implements use_leash(); at lines 796-801 the mounted-down branch applies the leash to u.usteed and spends a turn. apply.c:821-876 use_leash_core() sets mtmp->mleashed and obj->leashmon for a tame leashable monster (lines 833-860).

C turn path: nethack-c/upstream/src/monmove.c:1771-1774 dispatches tame monsters to dog_move(). dogmove.c:1011-1044 runs hunger/inventory handling, calls dog_goal(), then returns MMOVE_NOTHING when dog_goal() answers -2. dogmove.c:494-496 documents and implements that answer for mtmp == u.usteed.

Frozen JavaScript cause and counter-evidence: js/unported_monster_actions.js:297-305 admits starting-pet species but throws for monster.mleashed at lines 300-301; the same assertSimpleActionState() gates runSimpleMonsterAction() at line 1577 and the preflight action path. Yet js/dogmove.js:1314-1368 already handles the usteed setup and dog_goal() early return at lines 882-893. js/allmain.js:1219-1224 invokes preflightSimpleMonsterActions() before the live monster pass. Thus the unsupported-state check masks an implemented C-matching early return; the owner is the JavaScript guard, with dogmove.c:dog_move()/dog_goal() defining the safe exception.
